sources.title: Conductor

sources.finding: Vendor homepage presents a team of coding agents running in the cloud, isolated cloud workspaces, and shared workspaces where teammates can follow work and prompt together in real time. sources.title: Cloud FAQ
sources.locator: Features and plans; Cloud specifications; Security

sources.title: Conductor Cloud
sources.locator: Cloud Computer; Local and Cloud workspaces
sources.finding: Each agent runs in its own isolated cloud sandbox and keeps working after the laptop closes until the sandbox sleeps; "The chat, diff, git, terminal, and pull request workflow is the same in both" local and cloud. sources.title: Multiplayer
sources.locator: Shared chat; Home; Hand off a workspace
sources.finding: Cloud organization workspaces are shared with the team; transcripts update live; presence dots for active teammates and typing indicators in a shared chat; Home filters by teammate and project; follow and reassign workspaces; direct links. The page does not describe co-prompting, private workspaces, roles or plan limits. Page undated.

sources.title: Workflow
sources.locator: Workspace per shippable unit; Run agents independently
sources.finding: Workspace is the delegation unit; branch/PR is integration unit. GitHub/Linear intake and repository instructions are documented.

sources.title: First workspace
sources.locator: Repository; Make it runnable; Start work
sources.finding: Repository options: "Open project" (existing local repository), "Open GitHub project" and "Quick start" (new repository). Setup and run scripts; chats with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode; gh auth status check. No text on repositories without a remote or non-git folders. Page undated.

sources.title: Parallel agents
sources.finding: Independent branches or multiple agents sharing one checkout; shared-file collision risk is explicit.

sources.title: Cloud workspaces
sources.locator: Sleep and maximum lifetime; Forward ports; Sync
sources.finding: Four-hour inactivity sleep; 23h50m hard lifetime. Files/chat persist, processes stop and interrupted turns need resending.

sources.title: Diff viewer
sources.finding: Unified/commit-filtered diffs, line feedback and GitHub review comments. "Conductor recommends actions as a workspace moves toward merge. Use those actions to create a pull request, respond to feedback, fix checks, and merge". Page undated.

sources.title: Checks
sources.finding: Checks may include Git status, "Pull request metadata", CI and status checks, "Deployments", GitHub comments and review threads, and todos. Blockers: "Conductor may block or discourage merge actions when required work is still open, such as unresolved todos or failed checks", so enforcement strength is not established. Page undated.

sources.title: Todos
sources.locator: How todos work; Send todos to agent
sources.finding: Humans and agents use workspace todos; unchecked todos block merge; @todos exposes list to agent.

sources.title: Checkpoints
sources.finding: Checkpoints are stored locally as private Git refs, captured "Before each supported agent responds" (agents not named); restoring a turn deletes that turn and later messages and reverts code changes since. Page undated.

sources.title: Conductor API
sources.locator: Introduction; Quick start (for AI); Authentication; Endpoints; Routines; Cookbook; Tips
sources.finding: Beta HTTP API under https://api.conductor.build/v0 with an OpenAPI document; bearer API key; endpoints for projects, workspaces (create, get, rename, archive, unarchive, sleep), sessions, prompts, transcripts, cancel ("drop queued messages"), SQL and routines. Routines created through the API run a saved prompt in a fresh workspace on each webhook JSON POST. Cookbook: "messages sent while it works are steered into the running turn"; Tips: a queued prompt reports idle until its turn starts. Some 403s come from a proxy that rejects default client signatures (send a User-Agent). Shows a routine example with the `conductor` CLI. No SDK is documented on this page. Quick start (for AI) requires a Conductor Pro account to generate an API key. Page undated. Endpoint table: GET /v0/sessions/{id}/status "Whether the agent is idle, working, or errored"; POST /v0/sessions/{id}/cancel "Stop the agent's current turn and drop queued messages". Tips: "Always pass an explicit model" (workspace creation, POST /v0/workspaces) and "An optional effort field sets the thinking level for claude and codex sessions". No sidebar-section endpoint listed.

sources.title: Conductor MCP server
sources.finding: Beta hosted MCP ("Tools and input shapes may change"): OAuth limited to mcp:tools and one organization, or bearer API key. Tools include create_session, send_message ("Send or queue a prompt for a session"), cancel_session ("Cancel the current agent turn and discard queued messages"), get_session_status ("Get a session's current agent status", no values listed), list_models, list_messages (after cursor), get_message and run_sql. No routine or section tools listed. Page undated.

sources.title: Security and permissions
sources.finding: Cloud agents run in isolated Linux sandboxes hosted by Vercel and can use the workspace environment variables and secrets; repository files and session data are kept in Conductor-managed infrastructure. Local agents run with the user account permissions; approvals can be required for shell commands, file changes, MCP tool calls or web fetches. Page undated.

sources.title: Conductor 0.85.0
sources.finding: Routines run agents on a schedule or via GitHub action, in the cloud, so Pro and Team only (no webhook text on this page); private workspaces; favorite models sync across devices in cloud organizations; Cursor subscription sign-in for cloud workspaces; per-organization cloud agent connections; "Plans, screenshots, and attachments in .context now sync from cloud workspaces to your Mac"; experimental workspace status matrix. Model picker shortcuts change models, effort and speed.

sources.title: Agent modes
sources.locator: Supported controls; Plan Mode; Codex goals; Skills

sources.title: Isolated workspaces
sources.finding: Each workspace is a git worktree on its own branch; a branch can be checked out in one workspace at a time; states workspace isolation is development isolation, not a security boundary, and agents run on the Mac with user permissions.

sources.title: Harnesses
sources.finding: Four harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode. Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode are bundled; Cursor sessions use Cursor Agent through the Cursor API. One harness and model per chat tab. "Conductor is free to use. We do not bill or resell model usage." Page undated.

sources.title: Configure model providers
sources.locator: Harness auth; Claude Code compatible providers
sources.finding: Claude Code via CLI auth or API key mode (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or compatible providers (OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Bedrock, GLM); Codex via "Codex sign-in, an OpenAI subscription, or an API key" (CODEX_API_KEY) or gateway; OpenCode via provider credentials; Cursor via Cursor API key. sources.title: Managed settings
sources.finding: Provisional organization-controlled settings file on a Mac overrides user and repository settings (for example enterprise_data_privacy, default models, environment variables).

sources.title: Cloud Computer
sources.locator: Specifications; Builds; Setup scripts; Environment variables and secrets
sources.finding: Each cloud workspace runs in an isolated microVM with 8 vCPU, 16 GB RAM and 32 GB ephemeral NVMe. The Cloud Computer is the shared development environment for a Conductor organization; the page gives no Cloud Computer disk size; up to 50 GitHub repositories; successful builds seed new workspaces; saved secrets are hidden but exposed as env vars inside workspaces; an Admin workspace agent can edit install/setup scripts and run builds.

sources.title: Set up cloud
sources.locator: Requirements; Setup steps; Admin and credentials
sources.finding: Cloud onboarding: create organization, connect the Conductor GitHub App, add an agent credential (subscription token or API key), build the Cloud Computer, then work in an Admin workspace. Admins can add shared API keys that take precedence over personal keys.

sources.title: From issue to pull request
sources.locator: Starting a workspace from an issue; Creating the pull request
sources.finding: A workspace can be started from a GitHub or Linear issue and inherits its title, description and context; Create PR sends the diff and repository context to the agent to draft the PR. Issue-PR linking is not described. After the PR exists, use Checks and Diff Viewer "to respond to CI, deployments, review comments, and todos".

sources.title: Review and merge a workspace
sources.locator: Review flow; Checks; Merge and archive
sources.finding: Diff viewer, Review action (agent reviews diff), Checks tab; unresolved comments, failing checks and open todos are to be treated as blockers; merge, then archive.

sources.title: Privacy
sources.locator: Data storage; Telemetry; Enterprise data privacy
sources.finding: Cloud session inputs and outputs are stored on Conductor servers; local session data stays on the Mac (~/Library/Application Support/com.conductor.app); analytics and crash logs via PostHog, including OS and IP address. No export, deletion or retention text. Enterprise data privacy is local-only and "cannot be used in cloud". Page undated.

sources.title: Settings reference
sources.finding: Settings include tool_approvals_enabled, Codex tool_approval_policy (default or always_approve), default plan mode, review/PR/conflict prompts, git.archive_on_merge, enterprise_data_privacy.

sources.title: FAQ

sources.title: Testing

sources.title: MCP

sources.title: Conductor 0.77.0
sources.finding: Alpha multiplayer and API for Pro users; "Workspace notifications now show the workspace name instead of the branch name" (no client named); experimental cloud cost estimates include Codex usage; background tasks live for everyone. API alpha: "Available to all Pro users." No price stated.

sources.title: Conductor 0.78.0: Introducing Conductor Cloud
sources.finding: Cloud workspaces on isolated microVMs that keep running when the laptop closes; start by signing up for Pro and creating an organization; shareable links, presence and teammates prompting agents together in real time; API to manage cloud workspaces. Said the mobile app was "coming soon" on 2026-07-30. "To get started, sign up for Pro and create an organization." Billing "opens the Stripe billing portal". No price stated.

sources.title: Conductor 0.80.0: Stacks
sources.finding: GitHub stacks (cloud; local needs gh stack extension); cloud workspaces include the Conductor CLI and Chrome; cloud environment variables moved to Organization → Environment and "editing them no longer requires rebuilding your Cloud Computer"; GH_HOST respected for GitHub Enterprise.

sources.title: Conductor 0.82.0: Conductor MCP
sources.finding: Conductor MCP launched; cloud MCP servers; "Your Cloud Computer got more oomph - they now have double the disk space (64GB)"; low-disk warnings.

sources.title: Conductor 0.83.0: Auto port forwarding
sources.finding: Cloud auto port forwarding; one-click PR approval from the git panel; messages to sleeping cloud workspaces wake them; View deployment(s) button; added completion sounds; "Fixed notifications for workspaces in another organization opening the dashboard instead of the chat" (no client named).

sources.title: Conductor 0.84.0: Edit files directly in diffs
sources.finding: Edit files in diffs; effort change mid-chat for some Claude models; "Codex chats now retry automatically when OpenAI rate-limits a request" (no surface named); "Port forwarding is now off by default for each workspace"; PR links can open in GitHub or Linear (Settings → Git); 0.84.1 swaps cloud agent auth without restart; remote desktop control in cloud (experimental).

sources.title: Conductor 0.86.0: Share your loadouts
sources.finding: "Removed Codex goals and message queuing. Messages sent while an agent is working now steer it instead of waiting in a queue" (no surface named); answer Codex questions while it works (no surface named); context usage popover shows Claude account limits and reset times, matching Codex; cloud run scripts; private workspaces marked with a lock; fixes for OpenCode rejecting Always allow approvals and for "cloud plan approvals appearing successful when the workspace rejected the response". Improvements also: "Open pull requests in Graphite"; "Prompt links fill the new-workspace composer in your active organization." The Always allow fix is in the Fixes list.

sources.title: Conductor 0.87.0: Search across files, OpenCode 2.0
sources.finding: Routine GitHub trigger filters (label, author, base branch) and weekday schedules; OpenCode 2.0; "Create and delete sidebar sections from the CLI, API, and MCP in cloud organizations"; with the experimental status matrix enabled, indicators "show distinct states for routine runs, attention, errors, running pull request checks, and merged pull requests"; video thumbnails in chat; security fixes; setup scripts from shared cloud workspaces no longer auto-run on collaborators' Macs.

sources.title: Conductor 0.89.0: Sign in with ChatGPT
sources.finding: Sign in with ChatGPT for Codex; "Steer Cursor chats while they're running, in local and cloud workspaces."; PR view top card; merge blocked if the PR changed on GitHub; Codex tasks no longer stop on temporary rate-limit errors; custom OAuth MCP servers can use the Conductor callback URL. PR view: "open the Review row to add unresolved comments to chat, or the Checks row to re-run or fix failed checks."

sources.title: Conductor.build on the App Store
sources.locator: Listing header, version history and Information; iTunes lookup API record for id 6791228564
sources.finding: US App Store lists Conductor.build by Melty, Inc., iPhone only, free, requires iOS 26.0+. Current displayed version 1.1.3 is labelled 2d ago on November 7; no exact release date is inferred. History explicitly lists 1.0.5 October 8 and 1.1.0 October 23, with no year displayed. Store listing does not override the sign-up closure.

sources.title: Conductor todos
sources.locator: How todos work; Send todos to agent
sources.finding: People and agents add workspace todos. Open todos block merging; @todos sends the list to the agent.

sources.title: Conductor privacy
sources.finding: Local chats stay on the Mac; Cloud stores inputs, outputs and workspace state. App analytics include feature/model events and errors in PostHog. No telemetry opt-out is stated.

sources.title: Conductor Remote Control
sources.finding: Experimental feature: the Conductor iOS app pairs with a Mac by QR code and can browse and create local workspaces, read chats, send messages, pick models, stop agents and archive workspaces. Works with local workspaces only; the Mac app must be open, awake and online, both devices on the same account; off while enterprise data privacy is on; traffic is end-to-end encrypted through Conductor's relay.

sources.title: Conductor terms
sources.finding: The terms explicitly define the Platform as proprietary hosted AI automation software including client-side and hosted software. They retain vendor intellectual property and grant restricted platform access.

sources.title: Conductor Cloud runtime FAQ
sources.locator: Cloud specifications; data privacy; own cloud machines
sources.finding: Conductor provisions a Vercel sandbox for each Cloud workspace, keeps Cloud sessions on its servers, and does not yet support user-supplied cloud machines. Local sessions stop when the Mac closes. The plan-family section includes an outdated mobile-app coming-soon sentence, so this pass does not use it to reconstruct current commercial entitlements. The Enterprise description names automated user provisioning without specifying its protocol.

sources.title: Conductor Cloud organization onboarding
sources.locator: Create or select the organization; Add an agent
sources.finding: Members joining an already configured organization add their agent credentials as needed. Organization admins can additionally configure shared agent API keys for the organization; those keys override a member personal key for the same agent. Organization creation includes optional teammate invitations.

sources.title: Conductor is joining Meta, revised announcement
sources.locator: Struck-through shutdown paragraph; replacement paragraph; FAQ on continued use, export and data
sources.finding: The shutdown paragraph is struck through. Its replacement says development will continue; the FAQ says normal operation continues. Transfer to local and account export remain documented. The FAQ retains the no-sale/no-training statement but no longer sets deletion dates. The revision has no displayed date.

sources.title: Conductor 0.94.0 and 0.94.2
sources.finding: The 0.94.0 release is listed November 9, 2026. Its page adds an undated 0.94.2 subsection recording removal of the Cloud shutdown banner. The parent entry also records model and bug-fix updates. November 9 is not an established date for the 0.94.2 subsection.

sources.title: Conductor 0.93.0 historical transition
sources.locator: Opening wind-down bullets and export instructions
sources.finding: The November 4 release still lists Cloud read-only November 13, shutdown November 20 and local model/fix updates until early 2027. These historical plans are superseded by the revised announcement and 0.94.2 banner removal. It also documents transferring a workspace and chats to local.

sources.title: Install Conductor
sources.finding: The install guide provides Mac download/setup steps, explicitly excludes Windows/Linux, and requires GitHub and an agent provider. It does not state an existing-account-only restriction.

sources.title: Conductor pricing redirect
sources.locator: Redirect destination homepage; Get Conductor and download calls to action
sources.finding: The pricing URL redirects to the homepage, which advertises Cloud, desktop and mobile and links Get Conductor. No plan price table appears. This does not establish signup completion, upgrade eligibility or free-tier entitlements.

sources.title: Conductor Cloud FAQ
sources.locator: Features and plans; Cloud specifications; own cloud machines
sources.finding: Cloud access is described for Pro, Teams and Enterprise; Team signup is invite-only. The FAQ states no additional Cloud compute fee currently and plans usage-based compute pricing. Users bring subscriptions or keys. It also describes managed Vercel sandboxes and a planned self-hosted offering, without release dates. The mobile coming-soon wording is stale against the released iOS app.

sources.title: Configure model providers
sources.finding: Model usage is billed through the selected provider account, subscription, usage pool or key. Conductor does not bill or resell it.

sources.title: Conductor privacy
sources.locator: Data access, chat storage and analytics
sources.finding: Local chats remain on the Mac and model traffic goes to the provider. Conductor stores Cloud inputs and outputs; PostHog stores analytics. This reference does not provide a general retention period or a shutdown deletion schedule.

sources.title: Conductor FAQ
sources.locator: How does Conductor make money?; moving to a new computer
sources.finding: The FAQ calls Conductor a free tool and describes future collaboration charges, without plan entitlements. That undated wording does not resolve the Cloud FAQ plan gates. Migration Assistant or copying the named local app and provider directories is documented for moving chats.

sources.title: What is Conductor Cloud?
sources.finding: The Mac app supports local and Cloud workspaces. Local processes stop when the Mac closes; Cloud agents continue until sandbox sleep. The page still documents shared Cloud workspaces and setup.

sources.title: Conductor Multiplayer
sources.locator: Shared workspaces; shared chat; hand off; direct link
sources.finding: Cloud organization members share workspaces and chats, see presence and live output, follow workspaces, reassign work and open direct links. The current page does not impose the withdrawn shutdown restriction.

sources.title: Conductor.build App Store listing
sources.finding: The US App Store lists the Melty iPhone app as free to download, requiring iOS 26.0 or later. The displayed version is 1.1.3. Store download price does not establish Conductor plan entitlements or successful account creation.
